request.state: The Can language is being designed for AI to author custom company business applications. Its priorities include adoption, token economy, consistent operation notation and readable intended JavaScript output. Data/authority/invariants live in Given, guarded actions in When, and presentation in Then. Changes face no deployed implementation compatibility requirement. A capability currently defines typed service operations and their results; consumers import it, enqueue external effects with send, keep a typed delivery association and process final outcomes in completion scenarios. Contracts for partial streaming output, progress updates and cancellation remain undefined. Underlying workerd exposes HTTP fetch, text encoding, cryptography and streams; the Cloudflare hosted platform separately supplies services including storage, inference and durable workflows. Reusable JavaScript packages are available for standard-library implementation. The next application cases include LLM conversations; conversational Ollama with ComfyUI images, binding positive/negative text and dimensions once to node input identifiers; the SystemONE JEV classifier with its NOUL/choice/score result distributions; sorting email; and scheduled, bounded discovery of opportunities with citations and reviewed CRM promotion. A provider may lack another provider's output schema support, streaming, tool calls, resumability or targeted cancellation. Common transport/parsing/binary machinery need not be reauthored, while company-specific destinations, consulted sources, acceptance rules, authorization of actions and budgets belong to the application. There are no measured implementations of the alternatives. Choose an initial architectural hypothesis to exercise, without treating it as adopted grammar or demanding total vendor feature coverage.

boundary.instructions: Which initial boundary is most promising to test against those applications? Assess repetition, semantic consistency, fidelity to differing providers, ongoing connector effort and responsibility allocation between emitted code and shared libraries. Existing drafts are revisable, and none of the proposed approaches has demonstrated superiority.

criteria.generic: Build on ordinary capability imports and one common call/lifecycle system, extending that general system for partial results and stopping where necessary. Publish provider-specific interfaces instead of common AI/media domain interfaces. It avoids forcing providers into one shape and still shares execution machinery; application-level schema and request/result mappings can remain more repetitive when switching or combining providers.
criteria.shared: Publish common typed generation/classification/retrieval/media interfaces from the standard library, accessed with normal imports, while exploring common incremental/resumable execution semantics only where the examples require them. Declare adapter capability differences rather than pretending interchangeability. Reuse may shorten applications, but the shared contracts and missing-feature/lifecycle treatment still require careful design and maintenance.
criteria.dedicated: Introduce language-level declaration and execution forms specifically for models, decision classifiers and media workflows, including provider settings and workflow-node input bindings. Specialized forms may improve brevity and diagnostics, but expand the language's long-term semantics and require a clear relationship with its existing service invocation mechanism.
